sections.h2: Salt Lake County at a glance
sections.html:
No Utah county has more people. Salt Lake City is the seat, and the 2025 estimate of 1,220,916 follows a 2020 count of 1,185,238. Whether your house is in Sandy, Murray, Herriman, Holladay, Millcreek, Midvale, Taylorsville, Riverton, Bluffdale, South Salt Lake or one of the larger cities such as West Valley City, West Jordan, South Jordan, Draper and Cottonwood Heights, or out in Magna, Kearns or Copperton, one county tax system bills it. Every date and office below applies.

Earthquake questions come up in this valley because the Wasatch Fault follows the mountain front. Past foundation repair, chimney work or a seismic retrofit deserves a folder of receipts you can hand to the buyer.

Valuation starts with the Assessor, who appraises as of January 1 and completes the roll by May 22. About July 22 the Auditor mails each owner a Notice of Valuation and Tax Change. After that, three offices matter.

  • Treasurer sends bills, collects payments and administers relief. Visit 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, call 385-468-8300 or write treasurer@saltlakecounty.gov. Weekday hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For relief questions, press option 2 on the same number.
  • Recorder files deeds and other documents, in Suite N1-600 of the same building at 2001 S State St. Phone 385-468-8145.
  • Board of Equalization decides value disputes. It sits at 2002 S State St, #N3-300, with mail going to PO Box 144575.

Pay by November 30 and there is no penalty. A weekend or holiday pushes that to the following business day. By law, bills go in the mail no later than November 1.

  • January 1: appraisal and ownership are fixed for the year.
  • Around July 22: owners receive valuation notices.
  • August 1: appeals open at the Board of Equalization.
  • September 15: appeals close, unless 45 days after your notice falls later.
  • December 1: anything unpaid is delinquent.
  • January 31: the penalty rises when a balance remains.

The first penalty, charged December 1, is 2.5% or $10 per parcel, whichever is more. Clear the full balance by January 31 and it falls to 1% or $10, again the larger. Wait longer and it goes back to 2.5% with interest running from January 1. A December or January closing means asking escrow whether the bill is settled.

sections.h2: How the residential exemption works when a house sells
sections.html:
Utah knocks 45% off the taxable value of a primary home, leaving 55% of market value to tax. To count, the house must be someone's main residence for 183 consecutive days or more in the calendar year, whether the owner or a full-time tenant lives there. Each household gets one.

A new owner does not inherit the break. The buyer files a new declaration, using Form TC-473A starting January 1, 2027, by September 15 with the Board of Equalization. Without it the house may be taxed on 100% of market value that year. Mention it to your buyer when the contract is signed.

Disputes about value go to the county Board of Equalization, with September 15 as the yearly cutoff. Walk-in filings must arrive by 5:00 p.m. that day. Mail needs that day's postmark. Online submissions can be completed until 11:59 p.m.

  • Send the signed application and every exhibit to propertytaxappeals@saltlakecounty.gov, or mail the packet to 2002 S State St #N3-300.
  • Good exhibits: three or more recent comparable sales, a professional appraisal, proof of mistakes in county records, or your own purchase papers.
  • Bought within the window from July 1 of last year to June 30 of this year? Your closing statement is often the best proof.

Independent hearing officers review what you submit and recommend an outcome. The Board then raises, lowers or leaves the value alone. Keep paying on schedule while you wait, since refunds follow only a final ruling. If you disagree with the Board, the State Tax Commission accepts an appeal within 30 days.

Six Treasurer programs help owners who meet age, income or status tests. Forms open on January 1 and are due by September 1.

Treasurer relief programs and who qualifies
ProgramWho qualifies
Circuit BreakerAge 67 or older, or a surviving spouse, with household income up to $44,221
Indigent ReliefAge 65 or older or receiving disability benefits, with income and assets below $44,221
Senior DeferralHomeowners age 75 or older meeting income and asset rules
Disabled Veteran ReliefOwners with a service-related disability, or out-of-state active duty members
Blind ReliefLegally blind owners and certain survivors
Hardship ReliefExtreme hardship, subject to income and asset limits

Any deferral or relief claim on a house you are selling alters the payoff, so phone the Treasurer well before closing.

sections.h2: What happens when tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Ignore tax long enough and the county sells the property. Redemption ends March 15 in the fifth year after delinquency, and the Auditor then holds the final sale on the fourth Thursday of May. You may still pay right up until that sale.

A newspaper carries the notice for four weeks, and copies are mailed to owners and other interested parties. Facing this, request an exact payoff from the Treasurer. Closing a sale before redemption expires lets escrow settle the balance from your proceeds, often the tidiest way out.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Salt Lake County
sections.html:
Each recording costs a flat $40, and the paper must follow formatting and notary rules. Go to Suite N1-600 at 2001 South State Street on a weekday between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

  • Black print on one side of white 8.5 by 11 inch paper.
  • Leave a 2.5 by 4.5 inch blank box at the top right of page one.
  • Include the parcel serial number, the legal description and where the grantee lives.
  • Sign in ink, with a notary acknowledgment and a stamp that can be read.

A standard closing leaves all this to the title company. A deed signed elsewhere, like one passed between relatives, must meet the same rules.

sections.h2: Selling with a tax bill pending
sections.html: Until paid, property tax sits as a lien on the house, and the title company checks its status before closing. Pull together the newest notice, proof of payment and any relief or deferral papers. Remind the buyer to file the new declaration by September 15 if your home had the exemption. Selling for cash removes the lender, not the tax search, so tidy payment records help the closing move faster.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. If that day is a weekend or holiday, the next business day counts. Tax unpaid on December 1 is delinquent.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Salt Lake County value?
faqs.a: September 15, or 45 days after your valuation notice is mailed when that comes later. File with the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Does the Utah residential exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A buyer has to submit a new declaration, and a late or absent one can put the house at 100% of market value for the year.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Recording costs $40 flat, plus $2 for each legal description beyond 10. Copies of a recorded document are $2 a page.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax relief as a senior?
faqs.a: Possibly. Circuit Breaker relief covers ages 67 and up with income up to $44,221, and Senior Deferral covers owners 75 and older. Call 385-468-8300, option 2, to check eligibility.
